text: Follow-up to feature covering stash A9D74372 (Stage harvest docline hardening): (a) Direction 3 DEFERRED from that chore — change how the Stage harvest commit reaches the Ship feature branch so a Stage-artifact defect (beyond docline frontmatter, e.g. committed-file scope) cannot ride into a Ship PR. Options: Stage pushes its harvest commit to origin/main before Ship branches, or harvest lands via a dedicated delivery mechanism. Larger blast radius (branch/push topology, partly Ship-owned) — evaluate before implementing. (b) Upstream template drift: the docline frontmatter contract + pre-harvest lint gate were applied to the in-repo .github/skills/impl-plan/SKILL.md and harvest/SKILL.md, but the generating .tmpl sources live in the external autoharness repo; update them there (never via out-of-tree writes from this workspace, per Principle IV) so a regeneration does not overwrite the fix. Source: plan-review of docs/exec-plans/2026-07-02-stage-harvest-docline-frontmatter-hardening-plan.md, 2026-07-02.

Provision npm publishing credentials for @backlogit (EXTERNAL, human-only follow-up carved out of 080-S / stash 9140F65C in-repo slice): (1) provision the @backlogit org/scope on npmjs.org; (2) create an npm automation token with publish rights and add it as repo secret NPM_TOKEN. No agent (Stage or Ship) can perform these -- they require npm-org and repo-secret provisioning. Once done, the NPM_TOKEN presence guard shipped in task 080.001-T lets the release.yml npm-publish job's publish steps run automatically on the next release (no workflow change needed).

DIAGNOSIS 2026-07-04: Root cause of the v1.3.0 npm-publish failure (run 28488788268, job 84441217752) confirmed = npm error code E404 "PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@backlogit%2flinux-x64 - Not found / is not in this registry". The existing NPM_TOKEN authenticated successfully (npm built the tarball; no ENEEDAUTH/EOTP) -- 404-on-PUT is npm's signal that the authenticated account does NOT own the @backlogit scope. So the token is valid; the missing piece is that the @backlogit organization/scope is not provisioned under the token's npm account. Fix = create npm org named "backlogit" (claims @backlogit scope) owned by / with the NPM_TOKEN user as a publisher; then validate with a prerelease tag (e.g. v1.3.1-rc.1) which triggers release.yml and actually attempts publish (--access public already set; platform packages publish before the wrapper). No repo/workflow change required unless the "backlogit" org name is unavailable (then rename all 6 npm/*/package.json + release.yml publish loop to a new scope).

Until then, distribution remains via `go install github.com/softwaresalt/backlogit/cmd/backlogit@vX.Y.Z` and the GitHub release binaries; the npm-publish job stays a tolerated no-op (guarded, no red X once NPM_TOKEN guard is in effect). Source: operator 2026-07-04.

Migrate the backlogit Copilot CLI plugin install/binary-resolution off npm to GitHub Releases.

Context: v1.5.0 retired npm publishing from the release workflow (PR #205). But the plugin still resolves/runs the binary via npm: `plugin/.mcp.json` and `plugin/plugin.json` use `npx -y @backlogit/backlogit-mcp mcp`, and docs (docs/plugin-guide.md, docs/installation.md, README) document `npm install -g @backlogit/backlogit-mcp`. Since @backlogit/* is no longer published (NPM_TOKEN never provisioned / npmjs access lost), the npx path is unreliable or broken for new versions — v1.5.0 binaries exist only on GitHub Releases now.

Goal: make plugin install work WITHOUT npm, resolving the platform binary from GitHub Releases (SHA256-verified, cached), consistent with how the CLI install scripts already work.

Scope / tasks:
1. Replace the plugin MCP command (plugin/.mcp.json + plugin/plugin.json `mcpServers.backlogit`) so it launches backlogit without npx — e.g., a small cross-platform resolver that: (a) uses `backlogit` on PATH if present; else (b) downloads the matching `backlogit-{os}-{arch}[.exe]` from the latest/pinned GitHub Release, verifies against SHA256SUMS, caches under ~/.cache/backlogit/bin/, then runs `backlogit mcp`. (Mirror the existing npm-wrapper Tier 1/Tier 3 logic, drop the npm Tier 2.)
2. Update docs: docs/plugin-guide.md, docs/installation.md, README plugin section — remove npm/npx instructions; document the GitHub Releases resolution + the go install / binary-download alternatives.
3. Retire now-unused npm artifacts: scripts/package-npm.sh, the npm/ wrapper dir (npm/backlogit-mcp, npm/platforms/*), and any npm references in the harness/registry.
4. Keep SHA256 verification and platform matrix (linux/darwin/windows x64/arm64) aligned with release.yml assets.

Acceptance criteria:
- `copilot plugin install softwaresalt/backlogit` (or the plugin's MCP launch) resolves and runs the correct backlogit binary with NO npm/npx dependency.
- Binary is platform-matched, SHA256-verified against the release SHA256SUMS, and cached for subsequent starts.
- Docs no longer instruct npm install; the GitHub Releases path is the documented default.
- npm/ wrapper + package-npm.sh removed; no dangling references.

Priority: high -- the current plugin distribution path is npm-dependent and effectively broken for v1.5.0+.

Add a `backlogit update` CLI command for self-updating the installed binary.

Goal: give operators one canonical, exclusive update command so future "installs" that are really just version updates go through a single mechanism, instead of choosing between the curl install script, `go install`, or manual binary download.

Behavior:
- `backlogit update` -- detect the current version (internal/version), query the latest GitHub Release (softwaresalt/backlogit), and if a newer version exists, download the platform-matched asset (backlogit-{os}-{arch}[.exe]), verify against the release SHA256SUMS, and atomically replace the currently-installed binary. Report old -> new version.
- Windows self-replace: a running .exe cannot be overwritten in place; use rename-current-then-move-new (e.g. backlogit.exe -> backlogit.old, write new) and clean up the .old on next run.
- `backlogit update --check` (dry-run): report whether an update is available without applying it.
- `--to <tag>`: update to a specific release instead of latest.
- Update the binary at the location it runs from; fail clearly with manual instructions if that path is not writable.
- Optional `--source`: build+install from source via `go install .../cmd/backlogit@latest` when Go is available.

Acceptance criteria:
- `backlogit update` upgrades an older install to the latest release with SHA256 verification and a clear old->new report; friendly no-op when already current.
- Cross-platform incl. the Windows running-exe replace.
- `--check` reports availability without applying.
- Clear, actionable errors when the target path is not writable or the network/release lookup fails.

Relationship: shares the "latest GitHub Release lookup + SHA256 verify + platform match" infra with the plugin-off-npm migration (stash 60B8564F) and the version-diff enhancement (companion stash).

Enhance `backlogit version` / `--version` to show current vs. latest available version and whether an update exists.

Goal: when the user checks the version, tell them not just the installed version but whether they are up to date -- surfacing the available version and prompting to update.

Behavior:
- `backlogit --version` / `backlogit version` prints the installed version AND queries the latest GitHub Release (softwaresalt/backlogit) to show current version, latest available version, and an up-to-date / update-available indicator. When an update is available, hint to run `backlogit update` (companion feature). Example: "backlogit v1.4.1  (latest: v1.5.0 -- update available; run `backlogit update`)" vs "backlogit v1.5.0  (up to date)".
- Graceful offline behavior: the network check MUST NOT break or noticeably slow `--version` when offline or rate-limited -- fall back to printing just the installed version with a note that the update check was skipped. Use a short timeout and consider caching the last-known-latest.
- `--no-update-check` (or env var / config) to suppress the remote check for scripting/CI.
- JSON output includes current, latest, and update_available fields.

Acceptance criteria:
- Version output shows installed vs latest + update-available state when online.
- Offline/rate-limited: degrades gracefully (installed version only, no error, bounded timeout).
- A flag/env disables the remote check; default stays fast.

Relationship: shares the latest-release lookup infra with `backlogit update` (companion stash) and the plugin-off-npm migration (stash 60B8564F).
